messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout (project: text-gen, rollout_id: r-9c3) is seeing elevated error rates in eu-central-1. Canary variant v2.1-candidate returning 5xx for ~18% of requests over last 4m. Sticky fallback engaging and routing sessions to fallback variant v1.8-stable in eu-central-1.
jen: seeing the same in console — latency spikes and 5xxs around 13:47 UTC. Canary started at 13:30.
alex_sre: paging oncall. Paging @mike_prod and @sam_runtime. This looks like a variant compatibility issue, not infra.
mike_prod: on it, joining — can you drop the exact failing trace?
jen: pasting a quick sample from the dev logs: ```
[2026-03-15T13:46:52Z] req=0x7f3 status=502 model=v2.1-candidate kernel=attention-fast error="kv-cache-mismatch"
[2026-03-15T13:47:01Z] req=0x8a9 status=500 model=v1.8-stable traceback="ValueError: unexpected token type"
```
sam_runtime: interesting — history: v2.1 introduced a small change in the tokenization preproc which is incompatible with the older checkpoint that sticky fallback uses. When sticky fallback sends a session pinned to the older variant, the cached KV/state can be incompatible and cause 5xx.
lara_cs: any customer impact yet? CX pinged about increased errors for EU customers on streaming completions. Ticket #INC-4821 opened.
alex_sre: initial mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout to stop new canaries from being created. 2) Disable sticky fallback for this rollout so that traffic will fall back to regional generic fallback (which is cross-region and healthy) instead of the older variant. 3) If needed, rollback canary to previous artifact. Assign tasks.
jen: commands: ```
# pause rollout
redwoodctl rollout pause --id r-9c3
# disable sticky fallback for policy 'canary-sticky'
routingctl policy update canary-sticky --sticky=false --target=regional-fallback
```
mike_prod: running step 1 now. patching rollout to paused — response OK. new canaries will not start.
ops-bot: ACTION: rollout r-9c3 state -> PAUSED by mike_prod at 2026-03-15T13:50:02Z :gear:
jen: running step 2 to flip policy.
jen: routingctl reports policy updated, sticky=false. applying.
ops-bot: ACTION: policy canary-sticky updated: sticky=false target=regional-fallback by jen at 2026-03-15T13:51:10Z
alex_sre: monitoring metrics now. We should see requests pegged to the regional fallback pool (which is healthy) and 5xx rate should drop.
sam_runtime: also clearing session KV caches for canary sessions in eu-central to avoid residual mismatches: ```
cachectl evict --region eu-central-1 --sessions --match rollout:r-9c3
```
mike_prod: ran evict, got 200 OK.
jen: within 3 mins 5xx dropped from 18% -> 1.2% and p95 latency back to baseline. logs show new requests served by regional-fallback-v3 which is compatible.
lara_cs: customer impact: initial assessment - ~4200 requests affected across 12 tenants in EU between 13:36-13:50 UTC. Two paying customers reported degraded conversational sessions (stream truncation). CS has triaged and opened follow-ups; status page updated: "partial degradation for EU completions".
alex_sre: good. Next steps:
- keep rollout paused until model variant compatibility check completed
- create regression test that validates KV/cache compatibility across fallback variants for future rollouts
- postmortem with timeline and owner (oncall rotation)
- consider changing default sticky fallback to prefer cross-region fallback when variant semantics mismatch flagged

jen: assigning owners: postmortem owner = sam_runtime, regression test = mike_prod, CS follow-up = lara_cs.
ops-bot: NOTIFICATION: Pager cleared — mitigation in place, 5xx back to baseline.
mike_prod: quick note: while sticky fallback is valuable for session affinity, we need a preflight to verify tokenization/preproc compatibility. created ticket INFRA-1147.
sam_runtime: will draft the postmortem. tagging in @alex_sre for review.
alex_sre: nice work. final status: rollout paused, policy reverted to non-sticky fallback, caches evicted, customer impact logged and CS engaged. We'll reconvene in 1h for RCA sync. :white_check_mark:
lar­a_cs: (edited) CS will follow up with affected customers and escalate credits as appropriate.
jen: closing thread for now; keep alerts enabled and report any regressions. :mag:
